Rate limiting

The Acme API limits how many requests each API key can make. Limits protect the platform from bursts and keep latency predictable for everyone.

Limits apply per API key, not per IP address. Rotating keys does not reset your quota.

Default limits

PlanRequests / minuteBurst
Free6010
Team600100
Enterprise6,0001,000

Response headers

Every response includes headers describing your current quota:

X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 587
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1764201600

Handling 429 responses

When you exceed the limit the API returns 429 Too Many Requests. Retry after the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, with exponential backoff and jitter.

async function withRetry(fn, attempts = 5) {
  for (let i = 0; i < attempts; i++) {
    const res = await fn();
    if (res.status !== 429) return res;
    const wait = Number(res.headers.get("Retry-After") ?? 2 ** i);
    await sleep(wait * 1000 + Math.random() * 250);
  }
  throw new Error("rate limited");
}
Do not retry in a tight loop. Keys that repeatedly ignore Retry-After are temporarily blocked.

Requesting higher limits

Enterprise customers can request higher limits from the dashboard under Settings → API. Include your expected peak requests per minute and a short description of the workload.

We usually respond within one business day. Temporary increases for launches and migrations are available on request.

FAQ

Do webhooks count toward my limit? No. Outgoing webhook deliveries are not counted.

Are limits shared across environments? No. Test and live keys have separate quotas.

What about batch endpoints? Each batch request counts once, regardless of how many items it contains.
